model.title: Combine: Leonidas of Rhodes won 12 Olympic races. He was a famous runner.

parts.text: Main idea: Leonidas of Rhodes won 12 Olympic races
Extra detail: he was a famous runner

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Leonidas of Rhodes, who was a famous runner, won 12 Olympic races.

panels.title: Omitted pronoun
points: The wreath that he won was olive.
The wreath he won was olive.
Both are correct; that is left out

keywords.def: a clause that adds information about a noun, starting with who, which, where, when, whose or that
placed in the middle of a sentence
left out: the race (that) he won
a clause that makes sense on its own

questions.q: Combine with which: The olive wreath was light. It was made from a sacred tree.
questions.a: The olive wreath, which was made from a sacred tree, was light.

questions.q: Combine with whose: The athlete won. His city built him a statue.
questions.a: The athlete whose city built him a statue won.

questions.q: Add a relative clause: The truce ___ allowed safe travel.
questions.a: For example: The truce, which heralds announced, allowed safe travel.

questions.q: Core: write eight sentences about ancient Olympia, each with a relative clause (portal response box or exercise book)
Extend: find and correct five punctuation errors in relative clause sentences
Stretch: write one sentence with an omitted relative pronoun and explain what was left out
questions.a: For example: The race he loved most was the stadion. (that is omitted)

questions.q: Olympia, ___ the Games were held, was in southern Greece.
questions.a: B) where. Olympia is a place, so where.
B) The runner, who won, smiled.

questions.q: Write a relative clause with where
questions.a: For example: Elis, where athletes trained,
